rungs.title: Cycles of pure codimension p and the group Z^p(X)
rungs.note: Generalizes Mathlib's Weil divisors (coheight one) to coheight p.

rungs.title: Rational equivalence of cycles and the Chow group CH^p(X)
rungs.note: Needs divisors of rational functions on subvarieties; Mathlib has orders of vanishing (AlgebraicGeometry/OrderOfVanishing) to build on.

rungs.title: Smooth projective complex variety as a compact complex manifold
rungs.note: Mathlib has complex manifolds (Geometry/Manifold/Complex) and projective schemes; the analytification bridge between them does not exist.

rungs.title: De Rham cohomology of a smooth manifold
rungs.note: Differential forms on manifolds and the exterior derivative are missing from Mathlib; this is the largest piece of foundations.

rungs.title: Hodge decomposition H^k(X, C) = ⊕ H^{p,q} on a compact Kähler manifold
rungs.note: Needs Kähler metrics, the Laplacian, and elliptic regularity (or a Dolbeault-theoretic route).

rungs.title: The cycle class map cl : CH^p(X) → H^{2p}(X, Q) lands in H^{p,p}
HodgeInterface: cohomology, Hodge decomposition and cycle class map as a structure with cited axioms
rungs.note: Interface-first pattern (docs/harness.md). Axioms only as known theorems need them, each cited. Red team must show no axiom makes the statement trivial.

rungs.title: The Hodge conjecture stated against HodgeInterface, as a sorry-free Prop
rungs.note: Milestone M1. Target status is stated, not checked.

rungs.title: The cases p = 0 and p = dim X against HodgeInterface
rungs.note: Milestone M2, first case. Should follow from the interface axioms on H^0 and H^{2n}; if it does not, the interface is missing something and the rung says what.

rungs.title: Lefschetz (1,1): the case p = 1 against HodgeInterface
rungs.note: Needs the exponential sequence as interface data (Lefschetz1924, Voisin2002 ch. 7). Red team: the axiom must not simply assert surjectivity onto Hodge classes.

rungs.title: Hard Lefschetz as interface data and the reduction of the conjecture to 2p ≤ dim X
Statement: every rational (p,p)-class on a smooth projective complex variety is a rational combination of cycle classes
rungs.note: The unconditional statement: statement-interface with HodgeInterface instantiated from the foundations (milestone M3). Known cases to carry over: p = 0, p = dim X, p = 1.
